- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in recent days, model tends to overpredict; reduce forecast to reflect bearish pressure.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5+ points in 1–2 days); apply a 1–2 day lag correction to smooth out overreaction.  
- In absence of strong sentiment, model exhibits mean reversion bias — forecast tends to revert to recent 7–14 day average; use moving average as baseline.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period rallies (last 7–10 days); apply upward bias of 1–3% for final 7–10 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” values, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to reflect low conviction.
